NICHEROVER analyses for males

```{r}

data_iso <- readRDS("../data/data_iso.rds")

col4PCA <- c('MasterID','MainID','Trip','Sex','ProcedureYear','d13C',	'd15N', 
             'StandardLength_cm','ProcedureDate')  


PCAdata <- data_iso[,col4PCA] 
PCAdata$ProcedureYear <- as.factor(PCAdata$ProcedureYear)
m.PCAdata <- dplyr::filter(PCAdata, Sex == "Male") # Extract the data just for males , 48 males
m.PCAdata.PM <- dplyr::filter(m.PCAdata, Trip == "PostMolt")

clrs <- c("#aa6fac",
          "#4eb15e",
          "#168ece")
```

Analysis for Male NESE  Post-Moult

```{r}
row.names(m.PCAdata.PM) <- m.PCAdata.PM$MasterID


#First exploratory PCA with all data, including Isotopes
m.PCAdata.1.PM <- na.omit(m.PCAdata.PM)

# HCPC with 3 PCs
m.PCAdata.1.PM <- as.data.frame(scale(m.PCAdata.1.PM[c(6:8)]))

# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
hc.m.PM <- hclust(dist(m.PCAdata.1.PM, method = "euclidean"), method ="ward.D2")
hc.m.PM

plot(hc.m.PM, hang = -0.01, cex = 0.7)

# Check how many clusters there are 
res.nbclust.PM <- NbClust(m.PCAdata.1.PM, distance = "euclidean",
                       min.nc = 2, max.nc = 8, 
                       method = "ward.D2", index ="alllong")

# Agree that 3 is the correct number of clusters
# Compute hierarchical clustering on principal components
fit <- cutree(hc.m.PM, k =3)

plot(hc.m.PM)
rect.hclust(hc.m.PM, k=3, border="red")

# Add the Cluster to the original table
m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM <-  cutree(hc.m.PM, k =3)

f <- fviz_dend(hc.m.PM, 
               k =3,
               cex = 0.7,                     # Label size
               palette = clrs,               # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
               rect = TRUE, rect_fill = TRUE, # Add rectangle around groups
               rect_border = "jco",           # Rectangle color
               labels_track_height = 0.8,      # Augment the room for labels
               main = "Cluster PM - Males")

print(f)
ggsave(filename = "../figures/HC_Males_PM.pdf",
       plot = f,
       device = cairo_pdf)

# Bi-space
f <- fviz_cluster(list(data = m.PCAdata.1.PM, cluster = fit),
                  repel = TRUE,            # Avoid label overlapping
                  show.clust.cent = TRUE, # Show cluster centers
                  palette = clrs,         # Color palette see ?ggpubr::ggpar
                  ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
                  main = "Cluster PM Males")
print(f)
ggsave(filename = "../figures/HC_MalesPM_2D.pdf",
       plot = f,
       device = cairo_pdf)

## After the PERMANOVA analysis, we can confirm that PMC3 corresponds to PBC2, so we are going to change the names accordingly 

m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM[which(m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM == 1 )] <- 'Cluster 1'
m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM[which(m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM == 2 )] <- 'Cluster 3'
m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM[which(m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM == 3 )] <- 'Cluster 2'

#
write.csv(m.PCAdata.1.PM,'../results/Males_ClustersPM.csv')

################################################################################################################################################################################################################
```
Niche analysis 
```{r}


d <- 3
Psi <- crossprod(matrix(rnorm(d^2), d, d)) # scale

aggregate(m.PCAdata.1.PM[1:3], m.PCAdata.1.PM[4], mean)

# Generate parameter draws
nsamples <- 1e4
system.time({
 PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.PM), m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM,
                    function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.PM[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))
})



# Plot all mu 
pdf("../figures/PostMu_MalesPM.pdf")
niche.par.plot(PM.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = TRUE, plot.Sigma = FALSE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM.par), fill = clrs)
dev.off()

niche.par.plot(PM.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = TRUE, plot.Sigma = FALSE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM.par), fill = clrs)

# Plot all Sigma 
pdf("../figures/PostSigma_MalesPM.pdf")
par(mar = c(1,1,1,1))
niche.par.plot(PM.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = FALSE, plot.Sigma = TRUE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM.par), fill = clrs)
dev.off()

par(mar = c(1,1,1,1))
niche.par.plot(PM.par, col = clrs, plot.mu = FALSE, plot.Sigma = TRUE)
legend("topleft", legend = names(PM.par), fill = clrs)

# 2-d projections of 50 niche regions
nsamples <- 50
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.PM), m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.PM[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# format data for plotting function
PM.data <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.PM), m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM, function(ii) X = m.PCAdata.1.PM[ii,1:3])

pdf("../figures/NicheRegionsMalesPM.pdf")
niche.plot(niche.par = PM.par, niche.data = PM.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c(expression(paste(delta^{13}, "C")),expression(paste(delta^{15}, "N")),
                        'Standard Length'), col = clrs, xlab = expression("Variables"))
dev.off()

niche.plot(niche.par = PM.par, niche.data = PM.data, pfrac = .05,
          iso.names = c(expression(paste(delta^{13}, "C")),expression(paste(delta^{15}, "N")),
                        'Standard Length'), col = clrs, xlab = expression("Variables"))
#########################

# niche overlap plots for 95% niche region sizes
nsamples <- 10000
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.PM), m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.PM[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# Overlap calculation.  use nsamples = nprob = 10000 (1e4) for higher accuracy.
# the variable over.stat can be supplied directly to the overlap.plot function

over.stat.PM <- overlap(PM.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))

#The mean overlap metrics calculated across iterations for both niche 
#region sizes (alpha = .95 and alpha = .99) can be calculated and displayed in an array.
over.mean.PM <- apply(over.stat.PM, c(1:2,4), mean)*100
round(over.mean.PM, 2)

# Credibility Intervals
over.cred.PM <- apply(over.stat.PM*100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(over.cred.PM[,,,1]) # display alpha = .95 niche region

# Overlap plot
#clrs <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3") # colors for each cluster
over.stat.PM <- overlap(PM.par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = 1e4, alpha = .95)
pdf("../figures/NicheOverlapMalesPM.pdf")
overlap.plot(over.stat.PM, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = " PM Males Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")
dev.off()

overlap.plot(over.stat.PM, col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
            xlab = "PM Males Overlap Probability (%) -- Niche Region Size: 95%")

################################################################################
###############################   Niche Size   #################################

# posterior distribution of (mu, Sigma) for each strategy
nsamples <- 10000
PM.par <- tapply(1:nrow(m.PCAdata.1.PM), m.PCAdata.1.PM$ClustersPM,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = m.PCAdata.1.PM[ii,1:3], Psi = Psi))

# posterior distribution of niche size by species using the 75% contour to define strategy niche
PM.size <- sapply(PM.par, function(spec) {
  apply(spec$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = .75)
})

# point estimate and standard error
rbind(est = colMeans(PM.size),
      se = apply(PM.size, 2, sd))

# Niche Size
PM.size2 <- matrix(NA, nrow = 30000, ncol = 2)
colnames(PM.size2) <- c("Niche_Size", "Cluster")
PM.size2[1:10000,1] <- PM.size[,1]
PM.size2[1:10000,2] <- 'Cluster 1'
PM.size2[10001:20000,1] <- PM.size[,2]
PM.size2[10001:20000,2] <- 'Cluster 2'
PM.size2[20001:30000,1] <- PM.size[,3]
PM.size2[20001:30000,2] <- 'Cluster 3'

PM.size2 <- as.data.frame(PM.size2)
PM.size2$Niche_Size <- as.numeric(PM.size2$Niche_Size)

# Bhattacharyya coefficient to see how different the niche sizes are
# Create an empty matrix

Olap.PM <- matrix(NA,3,3)
colnames(Olap.PM) <- c('Cluster 1',
                        'Cluster 2',
                        'Cluster 3')

rownames(Olap.PM) <- c('Cluster 1',
                        'Cluster 2',
                        'Cluster 3')

for (sc in 1:3){
  for (sc2 in 1:3){
    Olap.PM[sc,sc2] <-  bhatt.coeff(PM.size[,sc], PM.size[,sc2])
  }
  
}

Olap.PM

median(PM.size[,1])
range(PM.size[,1])

median(PM.size[,2])
range(PM.size[,2])

median(PM.size[,3])
range(PM.size[,3])


plt.niche <- ggbetweenstats(
  data = PM.size2,
  x = Cluster,
  y = Niche_Size,
  pairwise.display = "none",
  xlab = "Clusters",
  ylab = "Niche Size"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = clrs)

print(plt.niche)

print(plt.niche)
ggsave(filename = "../figures/NicheStrategies_MalesPM.pdf",
       plot = plt.niche,
       device = cairo_pdf)
```
